end.summary:
Practised neutralisation in daily life, including ant bites, soil treatment, antacids and acid–base mixtures; examples were partly right but not steady yet.
Practised using hibiscus indicator colours to identify acidic, neutral and basic solutions; this was partly right and needs checking next time.
Practised that an acid and a base react to form salt and water and give out heat; this was partly right and needs checking next time.
Water added to acid was described as dilution rather than neutralisation; mixing acid and base being harmful was corrected later in the lesson.
end.parentNote: Khushi practised applying neutralisation to everyday examples and reading hibiscus indicator colours. They used the colour sequence to identify acidic, neutral and basic solutions, and later corrected the idea that acid–base mixing must make poison by saying it can form salt and water; the idea that water only dilutes acid still needs revisiting. At home, sort examples into “neutralisation” and “dilution,” and explain why for each one.
